table_description: IBM i system catalog view listing every table, view, and alias on the system. One row per relational object. Use it to discover what exists in a schema or to filter by object type. Large on systems with many libraries — always qualify by SCHEMA_NAME or TABLE_TYPE.

table_columns.name: TABLE_SCHEMA
table_columns.description: The library that owns the object (e.g. 'QGPL', 'QSYS2'). Equivalent to *LIB on the native side.

table_columns.name: TABLE_NAME
table_columns.description: The SQL name of the object. Distinct from SYSTEM_TABLE_NAME (max 10 chars, native).

table_columns.name: TABLE_TYPE
table_columns.description: Object type code. 'T' = table, 'P' = physical file, 'V' = view, 'A' = alias, 'M' = materialized query table. Filter to 'T' + 'V' for typical exploration.

table_columns.name: ROW_LENGTH
table_columns.description: Maximum row length in bytes. Helpful for sizing exports.

table_columns.name: NUMBER_ROWS
table_columns.description: Approximate row count as of last statistics gathering. NULL or 0 for views and brand-new tables. Don't trust as exact — for accuracy use SELECT COUNT(*).

table_columns.name: LAST_USED_TIMESTAMP
table_columns.description: When the object was last referenced. Useful for finding cold tables.

data_quality_notes: TABLE_SCHEMA / TABLE_NAME use the SQL (long) name. SYSTEM_TABLE_NAME holds the 10-char native name when they differ.
NUMBER_ROWS is statistics-based — newly inserted rows may not show until the table is reorganized or stats are refreshed.
Querying without a SCHEMA filter can scan a very large catalog on production-sized systems — always add WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = '...'.
